evidence.claim: Nguyễn Phú Trọng was General Secretary of the Party Central Committee and Secretary of the Central Military Commission; he had been State President from October 2018.
evidence.title: Biography of Party General Secretary
evidence.excerpt: Nguyễn Phú Trọng was General Secretary of the Party Central Committee and Secretary of the Central Military Commission; he had been State President from October 2018.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography directly lists the offices; useful for authority attribution even though it predates 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Background office inventory used to interpret 2022 authority
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Trọng as party leader; it shows party and military roles but not direct nuclear decision authority.
contrary_evidence: It is a 2021 biography, so it does not itself prove any 2022 action.
It shows that treaty/nuclear authority still sat with state organs, not the party chief alone.

evidence.claim: Ratification may be performed by the National Assembly or the President, approval by the Government, and accession by the National Assembly, President, or Government; treaty negotiation and conclusion are assigned to the President or Prime Minister under the law.
evidence.title: Law on Treaties, Law 108/2016/QH13
evidence.publisher: National Assembly of Viet Nam legal database
evidence.excerpt: Ratification may be performed by the National Assembly or the President, approval by the Government, and accession by the National Assembly, President, or Government; treaty negotiation and conclusion are assigned to the President or Prime Minister under the law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary domestic law with explicit competence rules; directly answers who can legally make treaty decisions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows formal limits on Trọng’s legal authority over treaty accession/ratification; he is not the named decision-maker in these provisions.
contrary_evidence: Vietnam’s party leadership can shape policy informally.
The law does not exclude de facto influence through the CPV system.

evidence.claim: Viet Nam is an IAEA member, party to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material, the Convention on Early Notification of a Nuclear Accident, the Convention on Assistance in the Case of a Nuclear Accident or Radiological Emergency, the Convention on Nuclear Safety, and the Joint Convention on the Safety of Spent Fuel Management; its national nuclear bodies are VARANS and MOST.
evidence.title: Country List: Viet Nam, Socialist Republic of
evidence.excerpt: Viet Nam is an IAEA member, party to the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material, the Convention on Early Notification of a Nuclear Accident, the Convention on Assistance in the Case of a Nuclear Accident or Radiological Emergency, the Convention on Nuclear Safety, and the Joint Convention on the Safety of Spent Fuel Management; its national nuclear bodies are VARANS and MOST.
evidence.source_locator: Country detail lines 1-123 and 1738-1739 equivalent country entries
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA legal and institutional status page; directly relevant to nuclear safety/security framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level institutional framework, not personal conduct; useful only for baseline exposure and safeguards context.
contrary_evidence: The page is current, not a 2022 snapshot.
It shows regulatory capacity but not ruler-level decision quality.

evidence.claim: Viet Nam signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty on 24 Sep 1996 and ratified it on 10 Mar 2006.
evidence.title: Status of Signatures and Ratifications
evidence.excerpt: Viet Nam signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty on 24 Sep 1996 and ratified it on 10 Mar 2006.
evidence.source_locator: status list entry for Viet Nam
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary CTBTO treaty-status register; exact dates are explicit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is state treaty posture, not a ruler-specific 2022 choice by Trọng.
contrary_evidence: CTBT is not yet in force globally, so this is commitment rather than complete verification architecture.
No 2022 ruler action is shown here.

evidence.claim: Viet Nam signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on 22 Sep 2017 and ratified it on 17 May 2018.
evidence.title: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.excerpt: Viet Nam signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on 22 Sep 2017 and ratified it on 17 May 2018.
evidence.source_locator: participant table entry for Viet Nam
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN treaty status page with exact signature and ratification dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State commitment, not personal conduct by Trọng in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The treaty is about abolition advocacy, not proof of direct risk-bearing authority.
It does not show whether Trọng personally drove implementation.

evidence.claim: The SEANWFZ Treaty lists Viet Nam as a State Party and establishes Southeast Asia as a nuclear-weapon-free zone with negative security assurances.
evidence.title: Treaty of Bangkok
evidence.publisher: United Nations Platform for Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zones
evidence.excerpt: The SEANWFZ Treaty lists Viet Nam as a State Party and establishes Southeast Asia as a nuclear-weapon-free zone with negative security assurances.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN treaty platform explicitly lists membership and treaty purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Regional treaty posture, not personal conduct by Trọng.
contrary_evidence: Membership does not indicate active 2022 ruler initiative.
The page is a general treaty description rather than a 2022 action record.

evidence.claim: Viet Nam submitted a memorandum on SEANWFZ-related activities as background documentation for the 2022 NPT Review Conference.
evidence.title: Memorandum on activities relating to the Treaty on the Southeast Asia Nuclear Weapon-Free Zone / submitted by Viet Nam
evidence.excerpt: Viet Nam submitted a memorandum on SEANWFZ-related activities as background documentation for the 2022 NPT Review Conference.
evidence.source_locator: record title, symbol NPT/CONF.2020/16, and conference background-document metadata
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN catalogue metadata is reliable, but the claim is about a background document rather than a policy decision authored by Trọng.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 background used at the 2022 NPT conference
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Viet Nam as a state participant, not personally to Trọng.
contrary_evidence: This is conference background material, not evidence of a new 2022 choice.
It does not identify Trọng as the decision-maker.

evidence.claim: Vietnam had considered nuclear power for years, but plans were cancelled in November 2016 and the profile shows no operating nuclear power reactors in the country.
evidence.title: Nuclear Power in Vietnam
evidence.excerpt: Vietnam had considered nuclear power for years, but plans were cancelled in November 2016 and the profile shows no operating nuclear power reactors in the country.
evidence.source_locator: summary lines 73-75 and nuclear power plans section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical secondary source; useful for country context, though it is not a primary government record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level program status, not a ruler-specific 2022 decision by Trọng.
contrary_evidence: The page is current rather than a 2022 archival snapshot.
Vietnam could still have nuclear-capacity planning and cooperation without reactors.

evidence.claim: Vietnam and the IAEA signed a Country Programme Framework for 2022-2027, and Vietnam said one priority was cooperating to promote the IAEA’s role in developing nuclear technology for peaceful purposes.
evidence.title: Vietnam, IAEA sign programme framework for technical cooperation
evidence.excerpt: Vietnam and the IAEA signed a Country Programme Framework for 2022-2027, and Vietnam said one priority was cooperating to promote the IAEA’s role in developing nuclear technology for peaceful purposes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable state-linked wire coverage of a clearly dated 2022 event; useful but not independent of Vietnamese official framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Vietnamese mission and ambassador, not to Trọng personally; still useful for the national policy line under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: It is peaceful-technology cooperation, not nuclear weapons policy.
It does not show direct general-secretary command over the file.

evidence.claim: At a side event of the 2022 NPT Review Conference, Vietnam said it always supports the use of nuclear technology for peaceful purposes and has fully fulfilled its obligations to the IAEA.
evidence.title: Vietnam backs use of nuclear technology for peaceful purposes
evidence.excerpt: At a side event of the 2022 NPT Review Conference, Vietnam said it always supports the use of nuclear technology for peaceful purposes and has fully fulfilled its obligations to the IAEA.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Clear 2022 event reporting from a reputable wire source; still mediated through state messaging.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is country diplomatic posture, not a direct personal act by Trọng.
contrary_evidence: Peaceful-use rhetoric does not demonstrate existential-risk reduction by the ruler.
It does not address any command-and-control or accident-prevention reform.

evidence.claim: Vietnam’s delegation at the 2022 NPT Review Conference emphasized support for nuclear disarmament, opposition to proliferation, and the right to peaceful nuclear technology use.
evidence.title: Vietnam contributes to promoting NPT’s role in global security
evidence.excerpt: Vietnam’s delegation at the 2022 NPT Review Conference emphasized support for nuclear disarmament, opposition to proliferation, and the right to peaceful nuclear technology use.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph 21 and related conference summary paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reliable 2022 conference summary, but still a mediated account of delegation remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Delegation-level stance only; no direct evidence that Trọng himself took a nuclear-risk decision.
contrary_evidence: Conference advocacy is not the same as implementation.
No direct ruler-specific authority or action is shown.
